The Phillips curve shows that there is an inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment in the short run. In other words, as unemployment decreases, inflation increases; conversely, as unemployment increases, inflation decreases.
In the long run, however, this relationship breaks down because wages adjust to changes in employment levels. The Phillips curve can be used to predict how much inflation will occur if the economy moves from one point on the curve to another. For example, if the economy is at point A (high unemployment and low inflation), then moving it to point B would result in higher inflation but lower unemployment.

To calculate the growth rate, you need to know the starting value and ending value.
The formula is:
(Ending Value - Starting Value) / Starting Value * 100%
Example: If your starting value was $500 and your ending value was $700, then your growth rate would be:
($700 - $500) / $500 = .4 or 40%.
This means that your investment grew at an average of 40% per year.
